text: Zalacaine is a strong inhibitor of HTX-5D.
Zalacaine is approved for use in adults only.
Zalacaine reaches peak plasma concentration about two hours after a dose.
Zalacaine does not require renal dose adjustment.
Zalacaine is stored below 25 degrees Celsius.
Venafil requires HTX-2C to form its active metabolite.
Venafil is taken with food to reduce nausea.
Venafil has a plasma half-life of roughly fourteen hours.
Venafil has no known effect on the QT interval.
Venafil is excreted mainly in the faeces.

Zalacaine's only relevant pharmacokinetic property listed is that it is a strong inhibitor of HTX-5D. Venafil's only relevant property is that it requires HTX-2C to form its active metabolite; it is excreted mainly in faeces.

There is no overlap: Zalacaine is not described as affecting HTX-2C (the enzyme Venafil needs for activation), and Venafil is not described as being cleared by or dependent on HTX-5D (the enzyme Zalacaine inhibits). No other shared mechanism (transport, absorption, excretion) is described for these two drugs in the information provided.

Therefore, based on the available data, no clinically significant pharmacokinetic interaction is expected between Zalacaine and Venafil.
